newsitem.title: INDIA: Mahatma Gandhi's ashes to be immersed in Ganges.
newsitem.headline: Mahatma Gandhi's ashes to be immersed in Ganges.

text.p: Forty-nine years after he was killed by a Hindu fanatic and cremated in Delhi, Mahatma Gandhi's ashes, kept in a bank vault, will be immersed in the Ganges river this month, Indian officials said on Sunday.
The nationalist leader was assassinated at a prayer meeting on January 30, 1948, five months after India gained independence from Britain.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the ashes, placed by Gandhi's aides in a State Bank of India locker in Cuttack, in the eastern state of Orissa, would be handed over to a close relative on Monday, following a recent Supreme Court order.
"The ashes will be formally handed over to Mahatma Gandhi's great grandson," a government official in the state capital of Bhubaneshwar told Reuters by phone.

PTI said great grandson Tushar Arun Gandhi was expected to collect the sealed wooden box after a court battle in which some politicians claimed the ashes were a hoax. They sought a chemical test but were denied that by the Supreme Court.

PTI said a special aircraft would fly the ashes in an urn to the city of Jabalpur in the central state of Madhya Pradesh. The urn will then be taken to several places across the country linked with Gandhi's non-violent campaign against British rule.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is to join a Hindu ceremony on January 30 when the ashes will be immersed at Triveni, regarded as the holy confluence of the Ganges with Jamuna and their mythical tributary, the Saraswati river.
Immersion of ashes at Triveni, near the northern city of Allahabad, is regarded by many Hindus as a sacred duty to the dead.
It was unclear what took so long for Gandhi's ashes to be handed over to his relatives. It could be simpler to explain why his assassin's ashes have also not been dealt with.
Relatives of Nathuram Godse, Gandhi's killer, say he had wanted his remains to be scattered over the Indus river, which flows through what is now Pakistan, when it again became part of India.
Both Godse and Gandhi had opposed the creation of Pakistan, though for different reasons.
